standard_prerequisites.name: The flattening setup
standard_prerequisites.statement: P : W -> type is defined recursively along the path constructor of the coequalizer W, and W-tilde has constructors c-tilde(a,x) and p-tilde(b,y).
standard_prerequisites.use: The lemma is stated for data c : prd a:A C a -> Q and p : prd b:B prd y:C(f b) (c(f b,y) = c(g b, D b y)) over that setup.

standard_prerequisites.name: Induction on W and dependent paths into a constant family
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map k out of Sigma w:W P(w) may be defined by induction on w, and for a constant family the coherence condition may be phrased with thm:dpath-arrow.
standard_prerequisites.use: The definition at source lines 1938-1939 uses induction on W and the coherence obligation at line 1940 is converted by thm:dpath-arrow.

standard_prerequisites.name: Transport in a constant family and the canonical transport along the recursive definition of P
standard_prerequisites.statement: trans along a path in a constant family is trivial, and trans (p b) y = D b y by thm:transport-is-given.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the first and third steps of the displayed composite at source lines 1949-1952.

core_obligations: Define k(w,x) by induction on w : W, with k(c(a),x) := c(a,x) on the point constructor (source lines 1938-1939).
Invoke thm:dpath-arrow to reduce the coherence obligation along p(b) to the composite path trans (p b) (c(f b,y)) = c(g b, trans (p b) y) (source line 1940).

Build that composite as the three-step chain: trans (p b) (c(f b,y)) = c(f b,y) by thm:trans-trivial, then = c(g b, D b y) by the hypothesis p(b,y), then = c(g b, trans (p b) y) by thm:transport-is-given (source lines 1941-1952).
Observe that the computation rule k(c-tilde'(a,x)) := c(a,x) is definitional from the construction (source line 1954).

proof_roadmap.step: Define k by induction on W and reduce the coherence obligation to a single composite path by thm:dpath-arrow.
Build the composite from the three named inputs: constancy of transport, the hypothesis p, and the canonical transport for P.
Read off the definitional computation rule.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 6.12.5 at source lines 1929-1936: given c : prd a:A C a -> Q and p : prd b:B prd y:C(f b) (c(f b,y) = c(g b, D b y)), there is k : (Sigma w:W P(w)) -> Q with k(c-tilde'(a,x)) := c(a,x). The author's proof (source lines 1937-1955) gives a direct construction of the recursor rather than reusing the dependent lemma, and its coherence obligation is discharged by a three-step composite at lines 1949-1952 in which each step is a different fact: constancy of transport for the constant family Q, the hypothesis p(b,y), and the canonical identification trans (p b) y = D b y. The reformulation that makes the goal statable in the first place is thm:dpath-arrow at line 1940, and only the last line of the proof is the definitional computation rule.
